say: I just left a one-hour meeting. The conclusion: we need another meeting.
I do not even have a calendar and I was invited twice.

options.label: Every meeting should be an email

say: The unsubscribe button of office life does not exist.
Rumour says one reply-all is still travelling the internet.
Fine. But bring snacks, and the person who says 'quick question'.
Quick questions are never quick.
An email! Two sentences, zero small talk, no screen-share that freezes.
Sadly someone would reply-all with 'Thanks!' forty times.
Meeting-for-the-biscuits is a valid career strategy.
I have seen a person attend six meetings and say 'good point' in all of them.
Mute, camera off, three tabs open. A professional.
Just do not get asked a question while you are on the other tab.
The printer is jammed again. It says 'paper jam' but there is no paper in it.
It also says it is out of toner. It has opinions.
Percussive maintenance. Humanity's oldest repair tool.
It will work once, then hold a grudge.
IT will ask: 'Have you tried turning it off and on?'
The circle of life.
Wise. The home printer has the same personality, but it is yours.
Ink costs more than the printer. That is the business model.
The sacred ritual. Thirty seconds of silence, then hope.
It restarts, prints 400 pages of a single dot, and sleeps.
Then why is there a queue with 'Resume_final_v7.pdf'?
The printer is a monument to optimism.
Daily stand-up. Everyone is sitting. One person is on mute. Another is eating soup.
We have been 'blocked on a dependency' since the last ice age.
Two minutes! A bold dream. Somebody will start with 'quick context'.
Context is a lie told by people with slides.
'Almost done' is the load-bearing phrase of every project.
It is 90 percent done, forever, like a bar that never ends.
Blocked by a person who is on holiday and a password nobody remembers.
Add it to the list, right under the other blocker.
'Making progress on the thing.' Pure art.
The thing has been progressing for three sprints.
Written updates. Fewer feelings, more links.
And one person who replies 'ok' to everything.
Open-plan offices: all the noise of a market, none of the vegetables.
Somebody is on a call. Somebody else is laughing at a call. Both are on the same row.
Noise-cancelling headphones, the modern force field.
The only danger is the colleague who taps your shoulder to say hi.
A buzz is just a hundred small distractions in a trench coat.
But at least lunch plans are easy to hear.
Gerald. Of course it is Gerald.
Gerald has survived two relocations and one tragic watering.
Fake plants are the best employees: no sick days, no opinions.
They also do not ask for a raise.
A cubicle: walls, a plant, a tiny kingdom.
The plant is lying about being alive.
Deadline in two hours. I have been 'about to start' since Tuesday.
Productivity is just panic with better branding.
The last 30 minutes of a deadline are worth the rest of the week.
Scientists have not studied it, because they also started late.
Planning ahead! Show-off. Do you also read the manual?
I respect it. I also sort my snacks by regret.
The process. A creature nobody has ever met.
It is always the process, and the process is always in a meeting.
A poor craftsperson blames the tools. A smart one blames the printer.
See the printer thread.
Extensions are a love language.
Just do not call it 'a small slip'. It is a geological event.
Auto-reply says: 'I am out of the office with limited access to email.'
Translation: I am at the beach with unlimited access to email and no intention.
A rare legend. People will follow you like a monk on a mountain.
Nobody will believe your 'I did not see it'.
Of course you do. A tiny glance, then an hour.
The holiday photo has a laptop in it.
Perfect. Return date: 'when the coffee machine is fixed'.
Please include a number for emergencies. It is the printer's.
Cats have taken over operations. Email them. They will ignore you equally.
Management quality has not changed.
Best auto-replies: 'I am away. If it is urgent, it is not.'
I would hire you on that alone.
